metadata.title: Tokyo dbt companies and people for the Tokyo dbt Meetup
metadata.purpose: Find Tokyo companies using dbt, and people who could speak at or attend the Tokyo dbt Meetup.
method: v1 (2026-10-01): v1 (2026-10-01): one research sub-agent. Read the Zenn API (dbt topic, ~800 newest and most-liked articles) and the Qiita API (dbt tag since 2024-06), kept authors writing in a company publication from 2024 onwards, pulled their Zenn bios, scanned Hatena tech blogs (Timee, LayerX, ZOZO, SmartHR, Money Forward), and read the dbt World Tour Tokyo 2026 and Coalesce on the Road Tokyo 2025 agendas. About 12 web searches plus ~20 fetches and API calls. Past chapter speakers added from enriched/tokyo-dbt-meetup.json by the assembler.

Lesson: The Zenn JSON API (zenn.dev/api/articles?topicname=dbt&order=latest&page=N) lists every dbt article with author and company publication in one call per page; the topic page itself renders nothing when fetched.
Lesson: The Qiita API (qiita.com/api/v2/items?query=tag:dbt) works without a token and returns the author's organisation.
Lesson: Hatena-based company blogs answer /search?q=dbt with server-rendered HTML, so Timee, LayerX and ZOZO posts were found without search calls.
Lesson: connpass blocks plain fetches (HTTP 403) and TECH PLAY returned 403, so Data Engineering Study and other connpass line-ups were not read.

Lesson: Tokyo women-in-tech events found (Women Tech Terrace by CyberAgent, PyLadies Tokyo, WiDS Tokyo @ IBM) had no data-platform or dbt talks on record; no women-in-data community line-up yielded a candidate.

v1 (2026-10-01): location pass. 22 people placed from public pages (Meetup hosts and RSVPs, GitHub, speaker bios, author boxes, recent in-person talks at a local-office employer) and LinkedIn search results (4 of them),, or from the same person's located record in another chapter's file, by the evidence rules in research/README.md. Each placed person has a 'location (high|medium)' note and evidence link. 24 people are still unknown.

v2 (2026-10-01): women-in-data pass with fetches only (no web search, about 28 fetches): Meetup gql2 groupSearch near Tokyo with 17 queries, then the past events of Women in AI Japan and Tokyo WiMLDS; connpass searches and group pages (PyLadies Tokyo, WTM Tokyo, ML女子部, GTUG Girls, Snowflake女子会 collaborations), the Snowflake女子会 note feed, the PyLadies Tokyo site and the WiDS site search. 20 people added (5 speakers and 15 connectors, 6 of whom also gave talks), plus organiser evidence for one existing person. Nobody's gender is recorded or inferred; no pronouns were self-published.
Lesson: connpass event and search pages now answer a plain curl with a browser user agent; earlier runs got HTTP 403.

Lesson: Snowflake女子会 is the most useful women-in-data community in Tokyo. Its connpass collaboration pages list all 11 organisers with employers, and its note.com feed (note.com/snowvillage_wmn/rss) has event reports with speakers. Its own events are on TECH PLAY, which returns HTTP 403.

Lesson: Meetup groupSearch near Tokyo returns mostly social groups for 'women'; only Women in AI Japan and Tokyo WiMLDS (one event, 2019) are women-in-data groups there. Japanese communities run on connpass instead.
Lesson: wids-tokyo.jp is now an unrelated site; WiDS Tokyo events are only on widsworldwide.org and connpass.

v3 (2026-10-01): company pass with fetches only (about 70 fetches): the green-japan.com dbt keyword search (8 pages, 160 ads) and one ad page per company, the Zenn dbt topic API (384 posts) and 24 post bodies, the dbt Labs sitemap (case studies and Japanese event pages), HN Who is hiring and findy-code.io.
Lesson: green-japan.com answers a fetch. The search page and each ad page embed __NEXT_DATA__ JSON with the work areas and separate work, requirement and welcome fields.
Lesson: findy-code.io ignores the keyword when fetched, so it returns every company.

v3 (2026-10-01): 1 LinkedIn profiles taken from pages already tied to each person (event, speaker and author pages, GitHub social accounts) with research/harvest_linkedin.py, without searching. Page links are medium confidence, GitHub links high.

field_definitions.companies.type: employer | consultancy | vendor | outsourcing | recruiter | community | independent | other
field_definitions.companies.watchlist: true for companies checked but not yet showing in-region dbt work (unconfirmed local presence, or weak/none dbt signal); kept so they are not re-researched
field_definitions.companies.excluded_from_outreach: true for companies deliberately not approached (e.g. dbt Labs staff who already speak regularly)
field_definitions.companies.local_presence: confirmed | not_confirmed | none — whether the company has people/roles in the region
field_definitions.companies.dbt_signal: strong = public post/case study/talk, or dbt required / core stack in a job ad; medium = dbt listed among alternatives, tagged by a job board's skill extraction, or seen only in a snippet; nice-to-have = listed as a plus; weak = unverified; none = stack appears to be non-dbt, or not applicable
field_definitions.companies.other_evidence.type: article | talk | case_study | oss | job_posting | careers | company_blog | conference_talk | meetup | podcast | news | profile | blog_scanned (blog checked, even if nothing relevant) | other
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.dbt_mentioned_in_: true = dbt seen in the ad text (or tagged from the text by the job board); null = only seen in a search snippet about the ad
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.posted_date: date shown on the job board (YYYY-MM-DD), null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.last_seen: last run in which the ad was still listed
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.job_family / work: as labelled by the job board (e.g. Analytics Engineer; Remote/Hybrid/On-site); null if not labelled
field_definitions.companies.people.id: kebab-case ASCII name, stable across runs
field_definitions.companies.people.city / based_in_region: city as seen publicly; based_in_region true = evidence they are in the region, false = evidence elsewhere, null = unverified
field_definitions.companies.people.level: leadership if the title contains Head/Director/VP/Chief/Founder/C-level/Manager/Lead, otherwise working
field_definitions.companies.people.confidence: High = name + title + company visible in a public source; Medium = indirect evidence; Low = weak evidence
field_definitions.companies.people.linkedin_confidence: high = name + company/role in the search result title; medium = indirect or name variant; low = searched, not found; not_searched
field_definitions.companies.people.profile_urls: other public professional profiles where the person can be reached, as [{type, url, source}]: type is one of github, meetup, zenn, qiita, velog, medium, devto, substack, ithome, sessionize, x, bluesky, website, note; source is the page that ties the profile to the person. never an email address or phone number
field_definitions.companies.people.mentions_dbt: true if any of the person's public content (or profile snippet) mentions dbt; false if content found without dbt; null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.speaker_pote: high = has given a dbt talk, 2+ public talks, spoke at this chapter before, or priority_tier 1; medium = some public content; low = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.attendee_pot: high = in region and public dbt content (or confirmed practitioner at a strong-dbt company); medium = in-region/unknown data practitioner; low = outside the region or weak identification
field_definitions.companies.people.internal_vinted: true for Vinted colleagues (kept for completeness, not outreach targets)
field_definitions.companies.people.priority_tier: 1 = strong recent lead: a proven speaker with a relevant recent talk, or an emerging_voice in (or not known to be outside) the region with authored content from 2024 onwards; 2 = good lead / needs verification / older content / relevant talk at another meetup; 3 = peripheral, off-topic or remote; organiser / backup / connector = special roles
field_definitions.companies.people.past_chapter_talks: talks this person gave at this chapter's own meetups, matched by name
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.type: talk | panel | podcast | article | case_study | oss | interview | organiser | host | post | profile
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.conten: stable id; an item with several authors appears under each of them with the same content_id
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.url_pr: direct = the item itself; overview_page = a listing/homepage where the item appears
field_definitions.past_meetups.talks.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.lead_type: proven_speaker = has given a talk, panel or podcast, or spoke at this chapter; emerging_voice = has authored public content (blog post, article, newsletter, open-source project, LinkedIn post) but no talk found yet — a priority for first-time speaker invitations; featured = only quoted or profiled in someone else's content (case study, interview, team feature); no_public_content = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.pronouns: pronouns exactly as the person publishes them (e.g. on a speaker listing, bio or profile headline); null when not self-stated. Never inferred from names, photos or third-person wording
field_definitions.companies.people.sourced_via: channels through which the person was found (list): company_blog_scan | case_study | conference_or_meetup_agenda | data_berlin_meetup | women_in_data_community | chapter_meetup_history | newsletter_or_blog | podcast | github | linkedin_search | job_ad_company_search | other

caveats: Titles, employers and cities come from public pages and Zenn bios, and are often inferred from the employer's Tokyo HQ — verify before outreach.
Many Japanese authors publish under a handle only; names are recorded as written (handle or Japanese name) and ids are ASCII slugs of the handle. Confirm real names before inviting.

Several blog authors are probably past chapter speakers under another name: okiyuki = Motoyuki Oki, Yoshi-ken = Yoshiken, harry/gappy = Harry, sisisin = Shimenyan, t-hiroto = Hiroto Takahashi, ryosuke839 = Ryosuke Lin Yamamoto, 栁澤 @i_125 (Qiita: Satoko Yanagisawa) = 'Yoshiko Yanagisawa'. These were left out to avoid duplicates; the last one suggests the chapter file may misspell her first name.
No women-in-data community source yielded candidates, and gender was never inferred. The organiser should ask the chapter hosts and Snowflake Data Heroes for introductions to balance the line-up.
No job postings were collected: the web-search budget ran out before the job-ad searches.
Only public professional information is recorded; no contact details. Pronouns only when self-stated (none found).

LinkedIn: 4 of 126 people have a profile url, taken word for word from search results. 122 were never searched (linkedin_confidence 'not_searched'); the 2026-10-01 pass searched the best-ranked leads with no known location first.
Speakers from women-in-data community events are recorded by where they spoke (sourced_via women_in_data_community). No one's gender is recorded or inferred.
Most Snowflake女子会 organisers publish under a handle; names are recorded as written, with the handle.
Job ads were read on 2026-10-01. Ads close, so check the link before quoting one.
